pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: mwifiex: Stop queues on close It's customary for drivers to call netif_tx_stop_all_queues() when the netdev stop operation is called. For some reason mwifiex does not do this. This happens to resolve a crash on a spinlock when doing "ifconfig mlan0 down; ifconfig mlan0 up". Signed-off-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:24053 TEST="ifconfig mlan0 down; ifconfig mlan0 up" on 8897/PCI-E Change-Id: I81b952691429f69d00f94c4d0b9bd8b6d5f3b414 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/176719 Reviewed-by: Ajay Gummalla <agummalla@chromium.org> Tested-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Bing Zhao <bzhao@marvell.com> Commit-Queue: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313252 Commit-Ready: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Tested-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mwifiex: WARN when resetting card When resetting the sdio card, log a warning using WARN_ON. This will tell us which path triggered the warning (mwifiex_tx_timeout vs. mwifiex_cmd_timeout_func). Additionally, it will enable us to track the frequency of the issue using UMA stats and crash reporting. Signed-off-by: Mukesh Agrawal <quiche@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Originally-reviewed-on: https://gerrit.chromium.org/gerrit/65639 [Forward port to 3.8 driver] BUG=chromium:270328 TEST=force reset (using gerrit.chromium.org/gerrit/38708), check dmesg Change-Id: I71aaf685a3f41c260a3dfb42e81d6e5cb458ff04 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/184171 Reviewed-by: Doug Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Commit-Queue: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Tested-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313253 Commit-Ready: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Tested-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mwifiex: Honor ASSOC_REQ_DISABLE_VHT If cfg80211 disables VHT, do not enable VHT IEs in the association or enable VHT block-ack parameters. Disable VHT for IBSS connections since cfg80211 cannot indicate whether to use VHT or not. Signed-off-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:352260 TEST=Run with and without modified wpa_supplicant to an 11ac AP with good connectivity. Observe with modified supplicant that VHT parameters are omitted in both association request and response and that "iw link" shows only HT rates. Ensure the opposite is true with ToT wpa_supplicant. Change-Id: I61ed22b1953850a2a0a6ece99c07fcf4de8a6d6a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/189888 Reviewed-by: Bing Zhao <bzhao@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: mukesh agrawal <quiche@chromium.org> Tested-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Commit-Queue: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313254 Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mwifiex: re-enable PCIe interrupt after awake event is received It's found that sometimes the PCIe interrupt isn't re-enabled in some cases where power save state is transitioning to awake state. It will cause cmd timeout and/or Tx watchdog timeouts if interrupt is disabled. This patch ensures that the interrupt is re-enabled. Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Bing Zhao <bzhao@marvell.com> BUG=chrome-os-partner:24397 TEST=browse to slashdot.org; open a new Ctrl-T console and run script: while sleep 10; do ping -f -c 100 www.google.com; done Change-Id: Id39f069af21daf1de5d1009ea59c5d5ca3db0cfa Reviewed-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/193353 Commit-Queue: Bing Zhao <bzhao@marvell.com> Tested-by: Bing Zhao <bzhao@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313255 Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mwifiex: Don't balk on corrupted IEs Some older APs may have trailing garbage in the IE data in probe responses. The beacon data is correct, and despite trailing garbage, the probe response is also correct. Instead of failing the association process due to the corrupt IE payload, we should allow the association process to proceed as well as it can, or at least validate whether it has enough data to succeed. Signed-off-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:395795 TEST=Manual: Associate with AP with symptoms of chromium:395795 Change-Id: Ibf935366d4d1cf3d6c7b16ebdc887e06885f024a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/211890 Reviewed-by: mukesh agrawal <quiche@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Tran <ntran@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Kiavash Faraji <kiavash@google.com> Tested-by: Kiavash Faraji <kiavash@google.com> Commit-Queue: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313257 Commit-Ready: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Tested-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mwifiex: fix TDLS wideband handling This patch fixes an issue where VHT operation IE construction would return failure even in case where TDLS wide band is supported. BUG=chrome-os-partner:24153 TEST=With all patches in this series applied on Clapper, test TDLS functionality. 1. run wpa_cli on peer device 2. Discover TDLS peer by command tdls_discover <Clapper WLAN mac address> 3. Setup TDLS link with clapper tdls_setup <Clapper WLAN mac address> 4. Teardown existing TDLS link tdls_teardown <Clapper WLAN mac address> From Clapper, DBus command can be used to setup TDLS link as follows: dbus-send --system --dest=fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 --print-reply \ /fi/w1/wpa_supplicant1/Interfaces/0 \ fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1.Interface.TDLSSetup string:<peer-mac-address> Change-Id: I72e0e8c45381a05dc348f65c77feab48a2aa73a0 Signed-off-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Bing Zhao <bzhao@marvell.com> Tested-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/207521 Reviewed-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/209549 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313258 Commit-Ready: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Tested-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mwifiex: move PCIe dump registers code to pcie.c file It has been observed that when command timeout occurs, PCIe specific code which reads PCIe registers is getting called even for SDIO based chipsets which leads to a crash. Timeout is gracefully handled and chip is successfully reset. The crash mentioned in the bug is now not seen with this fix. UPSTREAM: mwifiex: do not send key material cmd when delete wep key This patch fixes memory corruption reported by community developer. "Memory corruption occurs in mwifiex_ret_802_11_key_material_v1() when a short command response is received without a key length causing non initialised memory to be interpreted as the key length resulting in a memcpy() overwriting the part of the driver's private data structure beyond the key area." For v1 key material API firmwares, there is no need to send command to delete WEP key. WEP encryption/decryption is controlled by mac_control command. This patch avoids sending key material command in del_key case. Bug=None Test=Manual: Connect/disconnect to WEP enabled network. Change-Id: Ibd7f150f876979a0122b5d829054b42ff0c7dbf8 Reported-by: Martin Fuzzey <mfuzzey@parkeon.com> Signed-off-by: Xinming Hu <huxm@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Cathy Luo <cluo@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/236840 Reviewed-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/243820 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313362 Commit-Ready: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Tested-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: mwifiex: more_task flag for main_process This patch handles a corner case where TX packet would remain in driver queue till next packet comes in. Here is sequence: 1. TX packet is queued via hard_start_xmit and main_work is queued 2. SDIO interrupt comes in which directly call mwifiex_main_process. This starts executing main superloop. 3. Now work from step1 is scheduled but at first check itself it sees mwifiex_processing is set and exits. 4. Now if superloop from step2 has passed TX processing part of superloop this packet would remain in queue until next packet/command/SDIO interrupt arrives and queues main_work. This patch fixes this corner case by defining more_task flag which is set when mwifiex_processing is found to be true. At end of superloop we again check if more_task flag is set and if set, execute superloop again. BUG=chrome-os-partner:33858 TEST=Ran throughput test(iperf TX/RX) with all patches in this series applied, TP improvements seen around 25%. No Google autotest regressions. Change-Id: I77bb69c518367e2179a3b89e74414a6c52e55530 Signed-off-by: Shengzhen Li <szli@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Cathy Luo <cluo@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/260764 Reviewed-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/313368 Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: mwifiex: add SDIO rx single port aggregation This patch brings in support for SDIO single port rx aggregation to mwifiex. Maximum read size support by SDIO cmd53 is 64K. Based on multi port aggregation which is already part of mwifiex, idea here is multiple packets received in FW can be aggregated into single buffer. A separate upload type is defined for such packet aggregated to single port. Packets from this single buffer are later deaggregated into individual packets. This way, driver can receive more packets each time through single SDIO cmd53; thereby reducing no of times MMC bus is accessed. SDIO SP aggregation support is advertised by FW during load time and driver would get FW block size in command response of HostCmd_CMD_SDIO_SP_RX_AGGR_CFG. BUG=chrome-os-partner:33858 TEST=Ran throughput test(iperf TX/RX) with all patches in this series applied, TP improvements seen around 25%. No Google autotest regressions.
